title: Rabbi Eliezer ben Dehavai
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: A precious saying of his remains to us in Tractate Kallah Rabbati, end of chapter 2: “Whoever greets his teacher [as an equal], whoever says something he did not hear from his teacher, and whoever sets up a rival academy against his teacher causes the Divine Presence to depart from Israel; and whoever says something in his teacher’s name brings redemption to the world.” This statement is cited in Berakhot 27b, where the words “ben Dehavai” are missing.

notes.text: החולק על ישיבתו is rendered setting up a rival academy against one’s teacher, rather than merely debating the academy. Saved Davidson Berakhot 27b confirms the warning and lacks ben Dehavai as Hyman reports. The [as an equal] greeting gloss remains editorial.

The consulted Wikisource Kallah Rabbati 2:15 explicitly names Eliezer ben Dehavai and gives the warning and redemption clause. The consulted Sefaria Kallah Rabbati 2 passage instead has an unpatronymed Eliezer and a Ben Azzai formulation. These textual witnesses remain distinct; the greeting gloss is editorial.
